html:
SMTO-TSK-0014 — This task has newer work, so this action no longer applies

GUID: f57eb2da-6f4c-4555-9283-5d5b12dc092b
Slug: task-attempt-stale
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The task moved on since this page was loaded. It has already continued, been restarted, or been replaced by a newer attempt, so SMTO ignored an action aimed at the older one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page, or reopen the conversation from the Conversations pane. The page may still show buttons for an older attempt that has since been replaced.
  2. Scroll to the most recent reply in the conversation and use its buttons, such as Resume, Continue task or Restart task. Only the latest attempt of a task can be resumed, continued or restarted.
  3. Read the latest reply before acting, in case it already covers what you meant to do. The newer attempt may already include the change you were about to request.

What success looks like

  • The control on the latest reply works and the conversation shows the task carrying on from there.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't use buttons on older replies to restart or continue work that has already moved on.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The request targets a task attempt, request or command target that is no longer current: a newer attempt, continuation or child attempt now owns the conversation or run slot.

What this means

  • The request is not the current task attempt/head, a continuation already exists, or a command/advance target no longer matches current ownership and eligibility. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The request is not the current task attempt/head, a continuation already exists, or a command/advance target no longer matches current ownership and eligibility.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare current/latest request IDs, conversation head and existing continuation, retaining earlier attempt evidence.

How to fix it

  • The supplied attempt/request is not the lane head or has an existing continuation (or the command target changed before execution). Reload the conversation state and send the control to the latest attempt or child run; keep earlier results attached to their original attempts instead of re-targeting them.
  • Refresh the conversation and act on its latest task attempt. Keep prior results and unresolved effects attached to their original attempts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen control is bound to the intended current eligible attempt.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
